verses.text: Five days later, Ananias the high priest came down to Caesarea with some elders and a lawyer named Tertullus. They brought their charges against Paul to the governor.
When Paul was called in, Tertullus began to accuse him. He said, "Because of you, we have enjoyed a long time of peace. Your wise plans have brought many good changes to this nation.
Most excellent Felix, we accept this everywhere and in every way, and we are very thankful.
But I do not want to take up too much of your time. So please be kind and listen to us for a short while.
We have found that this man is a troublemaker. He stirs up riots among the Jews all over the world. He is a leader of the group called the Nazarenes.
He even tried to make the temple unclean, so we arrested him.
If you question him yourself, you will find out that everything we say about him is true."
The other Jews joined in the attack and said that all this was true.
The governor waved his hand for Paul to speak. Paul answered, "I know that you have been a judge over this nation for many years. So I am glad to defend myself in front of you.
You can easily check that it was no more than twelve days ago that I went up to Jerusalem to worship.
My accusers did not find me arguing with anyone in the temple. They did not find me stirring up a crowd in the synagogues or anywhere else in the city.
And they cannot prove to you the things they are now saying against me.

But I do admit this to you. I worship the God of our ancestors as a follower of the Way, which they call a false group. I believe everything that agrees with the law and everything written in the Prophets.
I have the same hope in God that these men have. I hope that all people, good and bad, will rise from the dead.
So I always try my best to have a clear conscience before God and before people.
After being away for several years, I came to Jerusalem to bring gifts of money for the poor of my nation, and to offer sacrifices.
I was doing this when they found me in the temple. I had gone through the cleansing ceremony. There was no crowd with me, and no trouble.
But some Jews from Asia were there. They should be here in front of you to accuse me, if they have anything against me.
Or let these men here say what crime they found me guilty of when I stood before the council.
The only thing they could say is that I shouted this while standing among them: 'I am on trial before you today because I believe the dead will rise again!'"
Felix knew a lot about the Way. So he stopped the trial and said, "When Lysias the commander comes, I will decide your case."
He ordered the officer to keep Paul under guard, but to give him some freedom. He also said Paul's friends could take care of his needs and visit him.
Some days later, Felix came with his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish. He sent for Paul and listened to him talk about believing in Christ Jesus.
Paul talked about living right, about self-control, and about the judgment that is coming. This made Felix afraid, and he said, "Go away for now. When I have time, I will send for you again."
At the same time, he hoped that Paul would give him money to set him free. So he often sent for Paul and talked with him.
After two years, Porcius Festus took Felix's place as governor. Felix wanted to please the Jews, so he left Paul in prison.
